nodes.label: D1: Server-authoritative tool rules
nodes.rationale: Decides per-block which tool breaks it via a common helper (BreakToolHelper + pure ToolSelector), following a strict priority order (unbreakable never, hardness-0 free, effective+correct tool first, main-hand fallback, then hotbar/inventory/offhand/backpack Tool Swapper candidates) so the mod never destroys a block without its vanilla drops and never gives more than vanilla would.

nodes.label: D2: Vanilla-equivalent durability, drops, hunger
nodes.rationale: destroyBlockAs is given the selected stack so mineBlock/hurtAndBreak (Unbreaking), Block.getDrops (Silk Touch/Fortune) and causeFoodExhaustion(0.005F) all mirror vanilla mining exactly, keeping the feature balanced rather than a free bonus.

nodes.label: D3: Capped mining delay instead of instant breaking
nodes.norm_label: d3: capped mining delay instead of instant breaking
nodes.rationale: delay = min(maxDelayTicks, sum of estimateBreakTicks) approximates vanilla's per-tick mining progress without efficiency/haste modifiers, capped at 40 ticks (2s) by default, so mass-breaking cannot become an instant-mining exploit while staying fast enough to feel like a bulk feature.

nodes.label: D4: Existing survival limits stay in force
nodes.norm_label: d4: existing survival limits stay in force
nodes.rationale: Blocks-per-click/axis, reach by power level, maxBlocksPlacedAtOnce, allowInSurvival, whitelist and tile-entity protection remain unchanged, plus new spawn-protection/adventure-mode checks, so survival breaking does not bypass any pre-existing anti-griefing/balance limit.

nodes.label: D5: Vanilla breaking cancelled while a build mode is active (survival included)
nodes.norm_label: d5: vanilla breaking cancelled while a build mode is active (survival included)
nodes.rationale: Keeps one consistent mental model: build mode on = mod breaks with its own rules (creative and survival alike); Disable = pure vanilla. Avoids a confusing hybrid where survival players could sometimes vanilla-mine and sometimes mod-break depending on tool state.

nodes.label: D6: Client preview and HUD for break plan
nodes.norm_label: d6: client preview and hud for break plan
nodes.rationale: Entries the client cannot find a tool for are flagged invalid and drawn grey instead of red; HUD near the crosshair shows tools and per-tool block counts plus a barrier icon for unbreakable-count, so the player understands why some blocks won't break without guessing.

nodes.label: D7: ServerConfig.survivalBreaking defaults
nodes.rationale: enabled=true, stopBeforeToolBreaks=true, maxDelayTicks=40, exhaustionPerBlock=0.005, centralizing the on/off switch and tunables in one place even though SimpleConfigValue is still an in-memory-only placeholder on both loaders (no file is read yet).

nodes.label: D8: Deliberate out-of-scope items
nodes.rationale: Automatic tool swapping into hand, inserting drops into backpacks, extra XP for delayed breaks, Disable-mode breaking beyond existing modifier behaviour, and config file loading were all excluded to keep the change scoped to the requested feature.

nodes.label: Root cause: Disable mode client/server desync after rejoin
nodes.norm_label: root cause: disable mode client/server desync after rejoin
nodes.rationale: ServerBuildState is session-only and reset by handleNewPlayer on join, but the client's static BuildModes.buildMode field survives leaving a world and was never re-sent on join, so client and server could disagree about whether Disable mode is active after a rejoin; fixed by BuildModes.resyncToServer() sending state on ClientPlayConnectionEvents.JOIN (T-S6).

nodes.label: Root cause: survival breaking always used ItemStack.EMPTY, no correct-tool check
nodes.norm_label: root cause: survival breaking always used itemstack.empty, no correct-tool check
nodes.rationale: BlockPlacerHelper.breakBlock always called BlockHelper.destroyBlockAs with ItemStack.EMPTY: no correct-tool check, durability, silk touch/fortune, or hunger; vanilla's requiresCorrectToolForDrops enforcement happens in Block.playerDestroy, which this path never went through, so a wooden pickaxe would silently delete diamond ore with no drop unless the mod added its own check.
